intro: People have played ball games for thousands of years. Long ago in Mexico, players used balls made of rubber. Later, games like soccer and basketball traveled across the world.
Games travel when people carry them. Sailors took soccer to new ports. YMCA teachers took basketball to new gyms. Written rules helped strangers play the same way.
Some sports need their own rooms. Wrestlers use a mat. Boxers use a ring. Fencers use a long strip. You will learn when each room got its rules and its dates.
bigQuestion: How do games and their rooms spread from one place to many?

timeline.t: Football Association writes soccer rules in London

James Naismith makes up basketball in Springfield
Fencing is part of the first modern Olympics
First World Cup is held in Uruguay
Judo joins the Olympics in Tokyo
First IHSA girls wrestling state finals

test.q: What were old balls in Mexico made of?
test.why: People in Mexico and Central America made rubber balls.

test.q: What did the Football Association write in 1863?
test.why: The Football Association wrote the Laws of the Game.
FIFA began in Paris on May 21, 1904.

test.q: Who took basketball to new gyms?
test.why: Naismith's students became YMCA teachers in other towns.

test.q: Where is the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame?
test.why: The Hall of Fame is in Springfield, where basketball began.

test.q: When were the first IHSA girls wrestling finals?
test.why: They came in 2022, at the end of the 2021–22 season.

test.q: What shape is a boxing ring?
test.why: A boxing ring is a square with ropes.
Kano Jigoro opened the Kodokan in Tokyo.

test.q: Which sport uses a long, narrow strip?
test.why: Fencing happens on a strip called a piste.

write.prompt: Pick one game that traveled and one sport room. Tell how the game spread, with one date. Tell what the room looks like, with one date.
tips: Name a year from the timeline.
